newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville details spring displacement power sales.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville details spring displacement power sales.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) has had only limited success in selling "displacement" power to operators of thermal generation units this spring, the agency said this week.

BPA has pushed to line up such sales, which entail idling of natural gas- or coal-fired power plants, ahead of an expected surplus of lower-cost hydroelectric power this spring and concerns that excess dam spills will harm endangered fish.

But many thermal plants are expected to continue operating through the spring since some, such as Colstrip in Montana, Centralia in Oregon and Bridger in Wyoming, are operated at higher rates during peak demand hours, but lower levels during off-peak hours, BPA said.
In a letter to an Oregon state Senator, BPA noted "selling power to mirror this type of operation does not help" its marketing or fish management efforts.
BPA also said many thermal plants are already out of service in the spring for regular maintenance work.
In addition, the agency said plant owners are hesitant to commit to fixed price contracts amid expectations of lower spot market prices as the runoff builds.
BPA noted displacement with resource owners in California and the inland Southwest was hampered by a lack of transmission availability into southern California.

The Pacific Intertie tranmission lines are currently capped at 5,200 MW, compared with a rated capacity of 7,900 MW, due to voltage concerns raised after two power blackouts in the West late last summer.

BPA said it is attempting, through the Western Systems Coordinating Council, to raise the intertie rating to 6,250 MW in time for the spring runoff and to capacity for the summer, but a final decision on the increase is still awaited.
